notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My research tools stopped working before I could read a single page.

I tried to open seven Proverbs 14 sources at the same time: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Wesley's Notes and Gill on StudyLight, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub, and the NET Bible notes. That request went over the tool's usage limit and returned nothing. When I tried Enduring Word again alone, the tool refused because I had no calls left for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and give a URL for every point. With nothing read, I have no verse notes I can back up, so I've left them all out rather than filling them in from memory.

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll fetch the sources one at a time. I'll start with the verse-by-verse ones (Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Precept Austin, Wesley). Then I'll look at the verses where the traditions might differ. Verse 14 (the "backslider") may show Wesleyan and Reformed views of perseverance. Verse 32 (refuge "even in death") may touch on the afterlife, and the NET Bible notes may cover how the Hebrew reads there. Verses 21 and 31 (kindness to the poor) may bring in Catholic social teaching, and verses 23–24 may come up in prosperity teaching. You'll get notes in the "v. 4: …" format, each with its URL.
